summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a history of coronary artery disease and Chagas disease was admitted with a three-day history of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and subjective fever. He was evaluated for possible cardiac or gastrointestinal causes, but ECG and cardiac enzymes were stable, and imaging showed no evidence of pancreatitis or abscess. CT and chest X-ray revealed small bilateral pleural effusions and trace abdominal fluid consistent with volume overload. Stool studies were negative for bacterial and parasitic infections, supporting a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis. His symptoms improved with supportive care, and he underwent scheduled hemodialysis. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue heart failure and diabetes medications, and follow up on abnormal labs showing transient leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated creatine kinase.
